title: NOT Inverter Gate (IC 7404)
summary: A NOT gate (Inverter) is a single-input logic gate that reverses the digital input signal (Y = A'). If the input is HIGH (1), the output is LOW (0), and vice versa.

images.title: ANSI Inverter Symbol
images.caption: ANSI Symbol for Hex Inverter with inversion bubble at output.

images.title: Breadboard Placement (IC 7404)
images.caption: IC 7404 Hex Inverter plugged across DIP center trench.

working_principle: When input A receives +5V (Logic 1), the internal NPN transistor turns ON hard into saturation, shorting the output pin to Ground (0V). When A is 0V, the transistor turns OFF, pulling the output up to +5V through a collector resistor.
applications: Complementary Signal Generation (e.g. Clock and Clock-Bar)
Square Wave Oscillator Circuits (Cascaded odd number of inverters)
advantages: Simplest logic function in digital electronics
common_mistakes: Confusing inverter bubble placement on inputs vs outputs.
Connecting output pins of two inverters together (causes short circuit).
quick_notes: Pin 14 is VCC (+5V), Pin 7 is GND.

viva_questions.q: How many inverters are inside an IC 7404 package?
What is the output of a NOT gate if the input is 0.2V?
viva_questions.a: Logic 1 (+5V), because 0.2V is within the LOW input range.

interview_questions.q: What happens when you connect 3 inverters in a closed loop?
interview_questions.a: It forms a Ring Oscillator that generates a continuous square wave clock signal.
